categories.main_business_segments: Dominion Energy operates through four primary business segments: Dominion Energy Virginia (regulated electric transmission, distribution, and generation in Virginia and North Carolina), Gas Distribution (regulated natural gas sales and distribution in several states), Dominion Energy South Carolina (regulated electric and gas utility in South Carolina), and Contracted Assets (nonregulated long-term contracted electric generation, primarily renewables, and a noncontrolling interest in Cove Point LNG). The company also reports a Corporate and Other segment for corporate functions and discontinued operations.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Dominion Energy's core technologies include large-scale electric generation (nuclear, natural gas, coal, hydro, solar, wind, and biomass), electric transmission and distribution infrastructure, and natural gas distribution and storage systems. The company is investing heavily in renewable energy technologies such as utility-scale solar, offshore wind, and battery storage, as well as renewable natural gas production from agricultural waste. Advanced metering infrastructure and grid modernization are also key production and operational methods.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company primarily serves residential, commercial, industrial, and governmental customers in regulated utility markets, with about 7 million customers across electric and gas services. Major end markets include retail electricity and gas consumers in Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, West Virginia, Utah, Wyoming, and Idaho, as well as wholesale electricity markets and long-term contracted power purchasers for nonregulated generation.
categories.geographic_coverage: Dominion Energy operates in 13 states, with core utility operations in Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, West Virginia, Utah, Wyoming, and Idaho. Its largest electric utility presence is in Virginia and North Carolina, while gas distribution is concentrated in the Midwest, Mid-Atlantic, and Rocky Mountain regions. The company also has renewable generation assets and contracted operations in several other states.
categories.supply_chain_position: Dominion Energy operates primarily as a downstream utility, delivering electricity and natural gas directly to end users through regulated transmission and distribution networks. In its Contracted Assets segment, it also acts as a power producer selling into wholesale markets or under long-term contracts. The company has exited most midstream gas transmission and storage operations through recent divestitures.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Dominion Energy's strategic focus is on expanding regulated utility infrastructure, accelerating the transition to clean energy, and achieving net zero carbon and methane emissions by 2050. Key R&D and innovation themes include large-scale renewable energy deployment (solar, offshore wind), grid modernization, battery storage, renewable natural gas, hydrogen, and advanced nuclear technologies. The company is also investing in energy efficiency, conservation programs, and digital transformation.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates the majority of its revenue from regulated utility operations, with rates set by state and federal regulators for electric and gas distribution and transmission services. Additional revenue comes from long-term contracted sales of electricity from nonregulated generation assets, capacity and ancillary services, and fee-based LNG terminal operations. Fuel and purchased power costs are generally recovered through regulatory mechanisms.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Dominion Energy is one of the largest U.S. regulated utility holding companies, with limited direct competition in its core service territories due to state regulation. In wholesale and contracted generation, it competes with other independent power producers and utilities. Major industry peers include Duke Energy, Southern Company, NextEra Energy, and Exelon. The company is positioned as a leader in clean energy transition among regulated utilities.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of 2021, Dominion Energy reported operating revenue of approximately $14 billion and net income attributable to Dominion Energy of $3.3 billion. The company has a large asset base (over $99 billion in total assets) and serves about 7 million customers. Its growth profile is driven by multi-billion dollar capital investment plans focused on regulated infrastructure and clean energy projects, with a strategic shift toward a higher proportion of earnings from state-regulated utility businesses.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Dominion Energy emphasizes safe, reliable, and affordable energy delivery with a strong commitment to sustainability and decarbonization. Its value proposition centers on providing essential utility services, leading the clean energy transition (including large-scale renewables and net zero targets), and leveraging regulatory frameworks for stable earnings. The company differentiates itself through its scale, integrated utility operations, and aggressive investment in renewable energy and grid modernization.
